result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers use a checkbox column and an action bar that appears only when rows are selected, and both handle rows hidden by filters well. A matches each action to its cost more closely: check-in, reschedule and cancel can all be undone, and a text gets one specific confirmation. A also covers fast selection more fully (Shift+arrows, Cmd+A, Cmd+Enter) and explains why the selection persists after an action. B's strengths are a bar that stays pinned while scrolling and good handling of partial failures, but cancel has no undo and its keyboard support is thin. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers use a contextual bar with a visible count, explain how hidden selections behave when filters change, and weigh each action by its consequences. B goes further on speed: it adds Shift+arrows, Cmd+A and Cmd+Enter, and it explains why the selection should persist after check-in. It also offers 'Show' and 'Deselect hidden' for hidden selections and adds Undo to cancel. A's partial-failure handling is a nice touch, but B covers more of the rubric overall. B spends a little length on filter chips and empty states, which drift slightly off scope.
